chapter.li: LEChapter54 Verse1 At the start of the 29th year of the judges, Ammoron sent a message to Moroni, asking him to exchange prisoners. VerseEnd Verse2 Moroni was overjoyed at this request, since he wanted the supplies used to maintain the Lamanite prisoners for his own people; and he also wanted his own people returned in order to strengthen his army. VerseEnd Verse3 Now the Lamanites had captured many women and children; but there wasn’t a woman or child among all Moroni’s prisoners, or the prisoners Moroni had captured. So Moroni resolved on a plan to obtain as many Nephite prisoners from the Lamanites as possible. VerseEnd Verse4 Therefore he wrote a letter and sent it with Ammoron’s servant, who had brought his proposal to Moroni.

Now this is what he wrote to Ammoron: VerseEnd Verse5 Ammoron, I write to 2PSF you a few words about this war 2PSF you’ve waged against my people, which was started by 2PSF your brother and 2PSF you’re still determined to continue after his death. VerseEnd Verse6 I want to tell 2PSF you something about God’s justice and the sword of His almighty wrath, which hangs over 2PSF you unless 2PSF you repent and withdraw 2PSF your armies back to 2PSF your own lands, or the lands 2PSF you inhabit, which is the land of Nephi. VerseEnd Verse7 Of course, I would explain it to 2PSF you if 2PSF you were capable of accepting it. I would explain to 2PSF you about that awful hell prepared to receive such murderers as 2PSF you and 2PSF your brother have been, unless 2PSF you repent and withdraw 2PSF your murderous aims and return with 2PSF your armies to 2PSF your own lands. VerseEnd Verse8 But since 2PSF you’ve previously rejected these things and have fought against the Lord’s people, I expect 2PSF you’ll do that again. VerseEnd

Verse9 Now we are fully prepared to defend against 2PP you; and unless 2PP you withdraw 2PP your aims, 2PP you will bring down on yourselves the wrath of that God whom 2PP you’ve rejected, resulting in 2PP your complete destruction. VerseEnd Verse10 And as the Lord lives, our armies will come against 2PP you unless 2PP you withdraw, and 2PP you will soon be killed. Indeed, we’ll take back our cities and lands, and we’ll maintain our religion and the cause of God. VerseEnd Verse11 But I suspect I’m wasting my time telling 2PSF you about these things, because I suspect 2PSI you’re a child of hell. Therefore I’ll end my letter by telling 2PSF you I won’t exchange prisoners unless it’s on the condition that 2PSF you turn over a man and his wife and children in exchange for one of our prisoners. If 2PSF you’re actually willing to do this, I will exchange. VerseEnd Verse12 But if 2PSF you don’t do this, I’ll come against 2PSF you with my armies, and I’ll even arm my women and children; I’ll come against 2PSF you, and I’ll follow 2PSF you all the way into 2PSF your own land, which is the land we first inherited. And it will be blood for blood, indeed, life for life. And I’ll engage 2PSF you in battle until 2PSF you’re annihilated. VerseEnd Verse13 I’m full of anger and so are my people. 2PP You’ve tried to murder us, and we’ve only tried to defend our lives. But if 2PP you attempt to kill us again, we’ll attempt to kill 2PP you. And we’ll try to recover our lands, the lands we first inherited. VerseEnd Verse14 Now I close my letter. I am Moroni; I am a leader of the Nephites. VerseEnd

Verse15 Now, when Ammoron had received this letter, he was angry, and he wrote another letter to Moroni. And these are the words he wrote: VerseEnd Verse16 I am Ammoron the king of the Lamanites. I’m the brother of Amalickiah, whom 2PSF you’ve murdered. I’ll avenge his blood upon 2PSF you. And I’ll come against 2PSF you with my armies, because I’m not afraid of 2PSF your threats. VerseEnd Verse17 2PP Your forefathers treated their brothers unfairly, so much so that they robbed them of their right to govern when it rightfully belonged to them. VerseEnd Verse18 Now if 2PP you lay down 2PP your weapons and place yourselves under our control, to be governed by those to whom the government rightly belongs, then I’ll have my people lay down their weapons and not carry on war any longer. VerseEnd Verse19 2PSF You’ve made a lot of fierce threats against me and my people. But we aren’t afraid of 2PSF your threats. VerseEnd Verse20 Nevertheless, I’ll gladly agree to exchange prisoners according to 2PSF your request, so I can preserve my food for my men of war. And we’ll carry on a war that will be eternal, either to bring the Nephites under our control and authority or to bring about their eternal extinction. VerseEnd Verse21 As for that God whom 2PSF you say we’ve rejected, we don’t know such a being and neither do 2PSF you. But if it’s true that there’s such a being, then it seems likely to us that He’s made us as well as 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse22 And if it’s true there’s a devil and a hell, then won’t He send 2PSF you there to live with my brother, whom 2PSF you’ve murdered, whom 2PSF you suggest has been sent there? But these things don’t matter. VerseEnd Verse23 I’m Ammoron and a descendant of Zoram, whom 2PP your forefathers seized and brought out of Jerusalem and forced into servitude. VerseEnd Verse24 I’m now a bold Lamanite. And this war has been waged to avenge their wrongs and to maintain and obtain their rights to the government. And so I end this letter to Moroni. VerseEnd

LEChapter55 Verse1 When Moroni had received this letter, he became even angrier, because he knew Ammoron knew what he wrote was a fraud. Indeed, he knew Ammoron understood what led him to this war against the Nephites wasn’t a just cause. VerseEnd Verse2 And he said: I won’t exchange prisoners with Ammoron unless he abandons his intention, as I stated in my letter, because I won’t give him any more power than he already has. VerseEnd Verse3 I know the place where the Lamanites guard my people, those they’ve taken prisoner. Since Ammoron refused to agree to the terms of my letter, I’ll attack them according to my words; I’ll pursue them with lethal force until they beg for peace. VerseEnd Verse4 When Moroni had said these words, he had a search made among his men to locate someone who was a descendant of Laman. VerseEnd

Verse5 They found one, named Laman, who had been one of the servants of the murdered king killed by Amalickiah. VerseEnd Verse6 Now Moroni had Laman and a small number of his men approach the guards who were over the Nephites. VerseEnd Verse7 They were guarded in the city of Gid; therefore Moroni had Laman, and a selected small number of men, accompany him. VerseEnd

Verse8 When it was evening, Laman went up to the guards who were over the Nephites. They saw him coming and called out, challenging him, but he said to them: Don’t be afraid! I’m a Lamanite. We’ve escaped from the Nephites and they’re asleep. And look, we’ve taken some of their wine and brought it with us. VerseEnd Verse9 When the Lamanites heard this, they gladly welcomed him. And they said to him: Give us some of 2PP your wine so we can drink. We’re glad 2PP you’ve brought wine with 2PP you because we’re tired. VerseEnd Verse10 But Laman said to them: Let’s save our wine until we go to battle against the Nephites. But saying this just made them want to drink the wine even more. VerseEnd Verse11 They said: We’re tired; so let’s drink the wine. Soon we’ll receive wine as part of our provisions, which we’ll drink before going against the Nephites. VerseEnd Verse12 And Laman said to them: Do as 2PP you wish. VerseEnd Verse13 They drank the wine without restraint, and the taste was to their liking; so they drank even more of it. And it was strong, having been prepared in its strength. VerseEnd

Verse14 They drank and enjoyed themselves, and before long all of them were drunk. VerseEnd Verse15 Laman and his men waited until they were all drunk and in a deep sleep, then they returned to Moroni and told him what had happened. VerseEnd Verse16 Now this was what Moroni had planned. Moroni had equipped his men with weapons, and he went to the city of Gid while the Lamanites were in a deep drunken sleep, and dropped the weapons inside to the prisoners, arming all of them, VerseEnd Verse17 even arming the women and all of their children, including anyone who could wield a weapon. When Moroni had silently armed all those prisoners, VerseEnd Verse18 even if they had awakened the drunk Lamanites, the Nephites could have killed them. VerseEnd Verse19 But this wasn’t what Moroni wanted. He didn’t enjoy murder or killing, but he took satisfaction in saving his people from ruin and death. In order to avoid any injustice himself, he wouldn’t attack the Lamanites and kill them while they were drunk. VerseEnd Verse20 However he had achieved his objective, since he had armed the Nephite prisoners inside the city walls and provided them with the power to control the city inside — VerseEnd Verse21 then he had the men accompanying him move back a pace from them and surround the Lamanite armies. VerseEnd Verse22 Now this was done at night, and when the Lamanites woke up in the morning, they realized they were surrounded by the Nephites on the outside, and that their prisoners were armed on the inside. VerseEnd Verse23 So they saw the Nephites had power over them. And in these circumstances they could see it wasn’t advisable for them to fight the Nephites. Therefore their chief captains asked for their weapons; and they brought them out and dropped them at the Nephites’ feet, begging for mercy. VerseEnd Verse24 Now this was what Moroni wanted. He captured them as prisoners of war and took over the city and freed all the Nephite prisoners. They joined Moroni’s army and added great strength to his army. VerseEnd

Verse25 He had the Lamanites he took prisoner begin to work on strengthening the fortifications around the outside of the city of Gid. VerseEnd Verse26 When he was satisfied with the fortifications for Gid, he had his prisoners taken to Bountiful. He also had that city guarded by a very strong force. VerseEnd Verse27 Despite all the Lamanites’ schemes, the Nephites kept and protected all the prisoners they had captured and defended all the ground they had retaken and advantages they had gained. VerseEnd Verse28 So the Nephites again began to be victorious and reclaim their rights and privileges. VerseEnd Verse29 The Lamanites attempted to surround them at night many times, but in these attempts they lost many prisoners. VerseEnd Verse30 And they attempted to provide wine to the Nephites many times, to kill them with poison or by intoxication. VerseEnd Verse31 But the Nephites weren’t slow to remember the Lord their God in these times of trouble. They couldn’t be taken in by their traps. They refused to drink their wine; indeed, they wouldn’t drink wine unless they had first given it to some of the Lamanite prisoners. VerseEnd Verse32 In this way they were careful that no poison was given to them. Because if their wine would poison a Lamanite, it would also poison a Nephite. So they tested all their drinks. VerseEnd Verse33 Now it was apparent to Moroni that they needed to retake the city of Morionton. Because the Lamanites had, through their work, fortified Morionton until it had become a very strong place of defense. VerseEnd Verse34 And they were continually bringing new forces into that city, and new supplies as well. VerseEnd Verse35 And so ended the 29th year of the judges’ rule. VerseEnd
